The `shutdownNow()` call returns a `List<Runnable>` of tasks that were not started, but the return value is discarded. In the previous code, when the worker was already shut down, `handleAlreadyShuttingDownWorker()` → `notifyQueueRunnables()` was invoked to send rejection/failure callbacks to pending requests. The new code path never notifies queued runnables, which means any in-flight client requests sitting in the queue will receive no response and may hang indefinitely.
Consider calling `priorityProcessWorker.notifyQueueRunnables()` after `shutdownNow()` (the `isShutdown()` assertion inside that method will be satisfied since `shutdownNow()` sets `running` to `false`), or explicitly process the returned list to invoke `onRejection`/`onFailure` on each `AbstractRunnable`.

The return value of `awaitTermination(30L, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` is a `boolean` indicating whether the worker actually terminated within the timeout. The code only catches `InterruptedException` but does not check or log the `false` (timeout) case. If the worker fails to stop within 30 seconds, execution silently proceeds to `killProcessIfPresent()` with no diagnostic trace. A `logger.warn(...)` when the return value is `false` would aid in diagnosing stuck workers in production.

I don't know how likely this scenario is but I suppose it's possible that after we set the `running` flag to false within the `AbstractProcessWorkerExecutorService` via the call to `shutdownNow`, an interrupt occurs while the service is completing the item it was running. In that situation I believe we won't call `notifyQueueRunnables()` because of the exception. What do you think about calling `priorityProcessWorker.notifyQueueRunnables()` before `killProcessIfPresent()` just in case? If the service already drained the queue then it shouldn't do anything.

I don't think it would hurt 🤔 

A side note, I wonder if `signalAndWaitForWorkerTermination` should call `shutdownNow()` 🤔

Good catch on the interrupt. 

I was worried about calling `notifyQueueRunnables()` while the executor is still running. I added a call to it if the `awaitTermination` returns success

Just curious, what's your concern about calling `notifyQueueRunnables()` while the executor is still running? I wonder if we should do the call right before the `killProcessIfPresent()` that way we handle the potential interrupt case here too.
